description: This line plot illustrates the relative change in performance (likely accuracy or efficiency) across different transformer model layers when applying two KV cache compression methods — LB-Avg and RULER4k — under varying token counts and bit precisions. The x-axis represents grouped model layers: Layer1-4, Layer5-12, Layer13-20, Layer21-28, and Layer29-32, indicating a progression from early to late layers. The y-axis, labeled “Relative Change,” is scaled from -15% to +5% in 5% increments, showing how each configuration deviates from a baseline (0% line, marked with a gray dashed line). Four distinct lines are plotted: LB-Avg of 2×tokens,8-bit (orange with circle markers) remains near 0% across all layers, slightly dipping to -1% in Layer13-20 and rising to +1% in Layer29-32; LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit (red with square markers) starts near 0%, drops to -3% in Layer5-12, then stabilizes around -2% through Layer29-32; RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit (light blue with circle markers) begins near 0%, declines to -3% in Layer5-12, further to -6% in Layer13-20, then recovers to -1% in Layer29-32; RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit (dark blue with square markers) shows the largest drop, starting near 0%, falling to -5% in Layer5-12, plunging to -15% in Layer13-20, then recovering to -10% in Layer21-28 and -2% in Layer29-32. A gray shaded rectangle highlights the 0% baseline region between Layer1-4 and Layer29-32, emphasizing the deviation of each method from the reference. The plot visually supports the paper’s claim that using more tokens at lower precision (e.g., 2×tokens,8-bit) yields more stable performance across layers compared to fewer tokens at higher precision (1×tokens,16-bit), especially in middle layers where the latter suffers significant degradation.
